name: 70,000 Light-Years from Home
rationale: Two-mana exile answers large counter creatures and unstationed ships; giving a basic to hand is a manageable drawback.

name: Andromedan Automatons
rationale: Multiple copies generate cards and station efficiently; one-toughness body trades poorly with Officer and Borg tokens.

name: Antagonist Incorporator
rationale: Excellent two-drop body; evasive artifact creatures and double-strike lord turn combat connections into a growing Borg board.

name: Assembly Specialist
rationale: Two artifact bodies enable Borg lords, sacrifice and station; individually weak without those payoffs.

name: Brad Boimler, Eager Ensign
rationale: Lifelink stabilizes; station triggers extra charge counters immediately, and attacking enhances subsequent counter placement.

name: Captain Benjamin Sisko
rationale: Cheap dilemma token engine with blue and black modal commons; five-color activated ability is a distant bonus.

name: Captain Jean-Luc Picard
rationale: Three-mana anthem plus recurring creature-and-ship cast tokens overwhelms boards; tokens themselves become 2/2s.
review_reason: Unconditional three-mana anthem and cast-token engine; supplied Fili the Pathfinder and Bards Company reached 66.26 and 64.09 percent with related but more expensive effects.

name: Command Decision
rationale: Answers grown counters creatures and active ships; draw mode prevents dead hands and triggers dilemmas.

name: Command Subadjunct
rationale: Cheap artifact pressure and lord support; vigilance permits attacking then stationing but one toughness remains fragile.

name: Conquest Mission
rationale: Nontoken artifact density supports a token engine; casting a three-mana enchantment first incurs substantial tempo cost.

name: Deanna Troi, Psychic Counsel
rationale: Efficient body and permanent team growth; extra counters on artifact tokens and Doctor synergies compound rapidly.
review_reason: Two-mana 2/2 with unconditional permanent creature growth; counter support is common and no extra mana is needed.

name: DOT-7 Repair Squad
rationale: Useful flying body; sorcery untap lets a creature station twice or station and remain available to block.

name: Dr. Beverly Crusher
rationale: Requires lifegain sources absent from its own body; Planet lifegain, Boimler and Neelix provide modest growth support.

name: Dr. McCoy, Surly Surgeon
rationale: Low immediate stats for four mana, offset by repeatable protection for an established counter board.

name: Emergency Medical Hologram
rationale: Cheap counter enabler and beam-up target; artifact Doctor typing helps Borg and federation but low standalone impact.

name: Excalbian Gamemaster
rationale: Large body with several Officers and death-counter redistribution; fixing increases token output without demanding a dedicated deck.

name: Federation Field Medic
rationale: Counter mode is reliable; ships and counter creatures frequently unlock the card-draw mode for beam-up value.

name: Federation Resupply
rationale: Tutor improves access to premium ships or Holodeck but costs tempo and does not itself affect combat.

name: Free Borg Revolutionaries
rationale: Landcycling prevents early clogs; five-mana body and team pump reward wide Borg or Officer boards.

name: Ghost of Illyria
rationale: Four-mana flier reuses removal artifacts or ETB creatures; can reset negative Auras and replenish counters.

name: Hologram Janeway
rationale: Solid artifact body; eight-power threshold counts all creatures rather than just attackers and is reachable on wide boards.

name: Malfunctioning Holodeck
rationale: Broad permanent exile with ward on an artifact; premium removal and synergy enabler despite prevalent artifact answers.

name: The Measure of a Man
rationale: Temporary exile buys two turns and a Clue; permanent eventually returns unless the Saga is removed before chapter three.

name: Miles O'Brien, Transporter Ops
rationale: Good body with immediate card draw when bouncing a cheap artifact; beam-up spells continue the end-step engine.

name: The Needs of the Many
rationale: Sacrifice requirement and two-mana reactive use are costly; strongest with disposable tokens against mass removal.

name: Oberth-Class Starship
rationale: Guaranteed Plains and artifact entry provide value; station six is expensive for only a 2/2 flier.

name: Peace in Our Time
rationale: Symmetrical optional draw rarely stops a profitable opposing attack; twelve counters make alternate victory implausibly slow.
review_reason: Reassessment: caster can draw immediately and every subsequent combat while declining attacks; this is a control draw engine despite symmetric optional access.

name: Pet Sehlat
rationale: Four power turns on eight-power attacks and stations ships; cannot attack alone and trades with ordinary three-power bodies.

name: Picard, Leading by Example
rationale: Sorcery pump accelerates station thresholds or evasive damage; a vulnerable two-drop requiring another body.

name: Primary Unimatrix Adjunct
rationale: Double strike makes every Borg and artifact flier lethal; four-mana body is modest if the artifact board is removed.
review_reason: Artifact-creature density supports double strike across multiple bodies; bonus has immediate combat impact rather than requiring another spell.

name: Pure Energy
rationale: Permanent counters support Doctors and Phlox; sorcery timing and beam-up replay tempo limit raw efficiency.

name: Rutherford, Upgraded Ensign
rationale: Finds removal artifacts or ships in artifact-rich decks; weak body and search misses matter outside those decks.

name: Saavik, Stoic Student
rationale: Own Vulcan and Advisor types contribute to an ambush; varied crew types can make this a removal spell plus body.

name: Set Phasers to . . .
rationale: Cheap defensive damage or offensive stun is useful; modal choice also grows dilemma creatures.

name: Shields Up!
rationale: Protects a growing creature or ship and leaves a counter; two-mana hold-up is a meaningful tempo burden.

name: Shuttle Ace
rationale: Attacking flier gains life and stations for four; five mana and losing flying on defense limit flexibility.

name: Sulu, Space Swashbuckler
rationale: Two-mana first strike is a sound floor; equipment and ships occasionally turn station or attack into a card.

name: Tactical Officer
rationale: Small initial body needs an established eight-power board; counters and untapping improve later attacks.

name: Test of Conviction
rationale: Two-mana permanent team pump punishes stalls with tokens; symmetrical draw mode offers emergency selection at a card cost.

name: There's Coffee in that Nebula
rationale: Finds lands or cheap engines and can reuse ETBs through beam up; spends mana without immediate board impact.

name: Troubling Tribbles
rationale: Zero-power tokens cannot block or station usefully without external counters or anthem; slow exponential growth has a very low floor.
review_reason: Zero-power nonblockers cannot station; requires external anthem or counters. Sarcophagus and Test of Conviction provide real but conditional rescue paths.

name: Una Chin-Riley, Number One
rationale: Large body helps reach eight power; first strike turns another attacker into a threat but requires untapping with a board.

name: U.S.S. Enterprise-A, Free Spirit
rationale: Three immediate bodies stabilize and help station a protected flying lifelinker; strong even before becoming a creature.

name: U.S.S. Excelsior, Cutting Edge
rationale: Removal plus eventual 4/4 flier; tapped restriction has ample targets because attacking and stationing both tap creatures.

name: Vexing Drone
rationale: On-curve artifact creature with tempo; enables profitable attacks and cheap beam-up reuse but does not remove blockers permanently.

name: Anthropological Mission
rationale: High spell-and-ship density can convert looting into cards; three-mana setup is weak when behind and creatures do not trigger it.

name: The Caretaker
rationale: Six-mana ward body stabilizes; recurring modal choices can steal a free spell, but it needs follow-up support.

name: Cetacean Ops
rationale: Ward and permanent growth reward noncreature sequences; four-mana 3/3 has a weak floor against efficient removal.

name: Cloak and Phaser
rationale: Usually costs five to seven mana for two bodies and filtering; distinct-land support is required to outperform normal creatures.

name: Cloistered Telepath
rationale: Cheap flash body improves hand quality, fills the graveyard and reuses well with beam up.

name: Consider the Prime Directive
rationale: Counter mode remains live early; tap-stun plus card mode is useful late and triggers dilemmas at instant speed.

name: Data, New Life
rationale: Two-mana creature grows every draw step; blue cantrips and modal draw effects quickly move it beyond common damage removal.
review_reason: First unassisted attack is only 1/2. The supplied Astonishing Ant-Man is a closer anchor than generic counter-text cards; artifact typing and mono-blue cost help.

name: Deep Space Scan
rationale: Six-mana draw spell needs many distinct lands; no board impact and double-blue cost make it vulnerable to tempo pressure.
review_reason: Six-mana draw amount is usually three or four, not six; distinct-land scenarios show five names is far from automatic.

name: Dominion Saboteur
rationale: Copies the best creature or artifact including its counters; active ships and grown creatures provide unusually strong targets.
review_reason: Omni-Changeling is 55.98 percent historically; copying counters and artifacts is valuable here, but five-mana cloning is not inherently a premium bomb.

name: Emergency Holographic Crew
rationale: Four-toughness artifact body faces a dilemma; surveil is reliable and ship recursion can make beam-up loops profitable.

name: Energize
rationale: Sorcery bounce is a tempo play with limited card value; beam-up mode can reuse friendly ETBs but costs substantial mana.

name: Ensign Pavel Chekov
rationale: Defensive body and possible stolen land; cannot accelerate land drops and often reveals no useful land among a small sample.

name: Enterprise NX-01
rationale: Stun creates a window to station; six charge counters are reachable but a 4/3 ship remains vulnerable to common removal.

name: Federation Probe
rationale: Cheap evasive artifact with modal ETB; excellent enabler for Borg damage triggers and beam-up replay, small alone.

name: Guidance Failure
rationale: Tempo removal for creatures or ships, discounted on attackers; target can be redrawn but answers counters cleanly.

name: Gwyndala, the Progeny
rationale: Two artifacts and a reusable Equipment token support artifact decks; copying other equipment has few high-impact targets.

name: Highly Illogical
rationale: Early counter hits important two-drops; four-mana unconditional mode is expensive relative to other interaction.

name: H.M.S. Bounty, Unlikely Timeship
rationale: Whale tutor can find Cetacean Ops or landcycling Whales; station eight delays both card draw and extra turn.
review_reason: Whale tutor is actual value, but five mana plus station eight plus a combat connection delays the extra-turn payoff.

name: Hoshi Sato, Exolinguist
rationale: Own Human and Scientist types ensure a small selection; five-mana 3/3 is inefficient despite a likely card.

name: Humpback Whales
rationale: Landcycling improves reliability; six-mana ground body is sturdy but lacks the evasive impact of ships.

name: Interstellar Effigy
rationale: Large artifact Man-o'-War creates a major tempo swing; an excellent beam-up and clone target.

name: Jett Reno, Problem Solver
rationale: Station supplies safe tap triggers and surveil; modal spells grow it toward repeated card draw.

name: Kobayashi Maru Scenario
rationale: Strong delayed resources are offset by a forced-loss fourth upkeep; reliable enchantment disposal is scarce in blue.
review_reason: Fourth upkeep can force a loss. Dahar Master sacrifices it, Ghost of Illyria resets it, Rules of Acquisition can donate it, and TPol can counter the loss trigger; none is guaranteed.

name: Lieutenant Commander Data
rationale: Grows from both players' noncreature spells and converts spare counters into cards; broad support with a low mana cost.

name: Lt. Cmdr. Geordi La Forge
rationale: Three-power body is acceptable and halves effective station demands; power depends on enough worthwhile ships.

name: Make It So
rationale: Two cards plus an Officer is solid stabilization for a draw spell; mode choice contributes dilemma triggers.

name: Marooned
rationale: One-mana lock on a tapped creature or ship; forbids beam-up escape but not other bounce or ETB value.

name: Melkotian Adjudicator
rationale: Cheap vigilant flier grows from modal ETBs and Tal Shiar attacks; vigilance contributes to station without sacrificing attacks.

name: Mr. Spock, Science Officer
rationale: Four toughness resists small damage and every draw becomes two; needs no dedicated combo to take over.
review_reason: Unconditional doubled draw steps on a four-toughness body need no additional setup; blue cantrips multiply value immediately.

name: Nyota Uhura, Communications
rationale: Excellent defensive stats; choosing common mana values produces occasional cards, especially two or three.

name: Open Communications
rationale: Cheap spell trigger and later ETB rebuy; card-neutral initial cast still spends mana without developing the board.

name: Romulan Bird-of-Prey
rationale: Cheap ship charges itself from noncreature spells and resists removal before activation; still needs time before blocking.

name: Rules of Acquisition
rationale: Stealing a bomb is powerful but giving three cards is costly; gifting a disposable token can be a safer draw mode.

name: Scotty, Miracle Worker
rationale: Recurring access to graveyard removal and draw with ETB creatures; requires both spells and a suitable returnable creature.

name: Seven of Nine, Unassimilated
rationale: Early 0/4 plus free filtering every turn; five distinct lands unlock cards but seven-land transformation is rare.

name: Starfleet Spanner Jockey
rationale: Cheap 3/3 blocks or stations immediately; spells enable attacks, but it is unreliable in creature-heavy builds.

name: Subcommander T'Pol
rationale: Flash body plus stun is a useful tempo play and dilemma; countering an ETB trigger sometimes produces a larger swing.

name: Suurok-Class Science Vessel
rationale: Replaces itself on entry and later flies; station five asks for support but meshes with noncreature-cast engines.

name: Suus Mahna Practitioner
rationale: Three-power station body with an eventual repeatable tap ability; common dual lands reduce the activation cost.

name: Test of Priorities
rationale: Card selection or ETB reuse at instant speed; modal synergy helps but neither mode provides unconditional advantage.

name: Those Old Scientists
rationale: Filtering followed by spell or artifact recursion; good graveyard setup, slow when pressured and weak with an empty graveyard.

name: V'Ger, the Intruder
rationale: Seven mana is substantial, but a large flying artifact draws on entry and attacks; fits green ramp and reanimation.

name: Vulcan Mind-Meld
rationale: Net one-card advantage from opposing library with unrestricted colors; supplies the opponent a card and costs early tempo.

name: Wesley Crusher, Starfleet Cadet
rationale: Flash modal value is flexible but modes are conditional; four mana for a 2/2 requires a useful bounce or counter target.
review_reason: Two conditional modes do not equal unconditional two-card advantage; counter mode misses creatures and bounce is capped at mana value two.

name: Zefram Cochrane, Warp Pioneer
rationale: Topdeck artifact access provides sustained advantage and free ship counters; efficient body works even before engines assemble.

name: Armus, Skin of Evil
rationale: Three-mana instant -4/-4 discard mode makes an excellent floor; late menace threat and repeated discard provide flexibility.

name: Assault Drone
rationale: Borg anthem includes itself for a 3/4 floor; boosts evasive artifacts and disposable tokens toward profitable attacks.

name: Automated Warfare System
rationale: Three-mana flying artifact turns spare tokens, Food or spent utility artifacts into cards while attacking.

name: Bat'leth
rationale: Immediate -2/-2 hits many utility creatures; persistent Equipment boosts evasive threats and station contributions.

name: Battle-Scarred Survivalist
rationale: Menace grows from any other creature dying, once each turn; initially small but token trades provide reliable support.

name: Blastoneuron
rationale: Flying body reuses a cheap dead creature's ETB and drains; beam-up and graveyard exile provide further triggers.
review_reason: Temporary graveyard copy is not permanent reanimation or opposing-creature exile; ETB reuse and flying still give genuine value.

name: Cha'DIch Investigator
rationale: Six power across two bodies, including a hasty Klingon; useful sacrifice fodder and efficient eight-power support.

name: Collation Trimatrix
rationale: Cheap artifact with a repeatable card engine; tokens and vigilance help pay tapping costs without losing combat pressure.

name: Collective Drone
rationale: Grows into a large station contributor with Borg tokens; two toughness makes it fragile without counters or lords.

name: Commander Raffi Musiker
rationale: Modal three-drop gives a Clue and graveyard options; repeated beam-up creates cards and dilemma triggers.

name: D'Ghor Bloodletter
rationale: Choice of token sweeper or symmetric sacrifice; 2/2 body and expendable Borg/Officer tokens reduce the sacrifice cost.

name: Death Is Irrelevant
rationale: Eight-mana repeated reanimation is devastating if reached; expensive enchantment does little against fast openings before then.
review_reason: Eight-mana enchantment carries a large early dead-card cost despite immediate end-step reanimation.

name: The Destruction of Praxis
rationale: Potential sweeper with scalable size; mixed mana bases increase coverage but often leave larger creatures alive.

name: De-evolve
rationale: Cheap blocker suppression, eventually exile; does not disable stationing or utility abilities and counters can overcome -4 power.

name: Eject the Warp Core
rationale: Instant two-mana removal scales to -6/-6 with abundant artifact or creature fodder; small mode often suffices.

name: Elim Garak, Simple Tailor
rationale: Efficient menace body with repeatable drain; modal creatures, instants and Tal Shiar attacks support frequent triggers.

name: Fugitive Listener
rationale: Three-power discard body pressures resources and stations ships; strong beam-up target, vulnerable to tokens in combat.

name: Gabriel Lorca, Mirror Menace
rationale: Large menace body returns from graveyard via dilemma; repeated use rewards modal density but five-mana curve remains a cost.

name: General Chang, Cold Warrior
rationale: Low-cost sacrifice outlet grows Klingons permanently; narrow tribal requirement and a small initial body limit broader value.

name: Georgiou, Terran Emperor
rationale: Immediate end-step card and huge defensive body; repeated life loss is dangerous but low-life token production can reverse games.

name: A Good Day to Die
rationale: Cheap power boost only replaces itself if the creature dies; competing removal and permanent buffs are generally stronger.

name: Grand Nagus Zek
rationale: Death-trigger Treasures grow the body and fix mana; only once per turn but token trades make activation easy.

name: Gul Dukat, Colonial Prefect
rationale: Seven mana and triple black are difficult; menace plus doubled life loss and gain can stabilize or finish immediately.

name: He's Dead, Jim
rationale: Unconditional instant creature removal with selection; cannot target unstationed ships but removes most active threats.

name: Hive Mind Coprocessor
rationale: Artifact creatures become card-draw threats immediately; evasive artifact commons and token swarms create multiple triggers.
review_reason: Numerous evasive artifact commons and tokens make team combat-damage card draw more credible than the generic text model suggests.

name: Impossible Choice
rationale: Instant draw mode is useful; removal leaves two blockers so weak against token payoffs, but dilemma flexibility is valuable.

name: In the Pale Moonlight
rationale: Nontoken sacrifice dodges Officer fodder, then Clue and bodies deliver value; five mana and delayed chapters cost tempo.

name: Kai Winn, Faithless Leader
rationale: Three-power two-drop trades with tokens; naming has limited information and does not actually prevent the opposing spell.

name: Khan, Vengeful Heart
rationale: Four-mana five-power threat converts a cheap artifact or token into two cards; recast from exile punishes some removal.

name: Obsidian Order Operative
rationale: Five toughness defends well and drains with dilemmas; limited offensive impact and four-mana cost constrain inclusion.

name: Organic Avulsion Unit
rationale: Menace gives artifact swarms reach in stalled games; modest body and activation cost make it dependent on board width.

name: Overflow Submatrix
rationale: Good three-mana body and recurring artifact creatures; cheap ETB artifacts, sacrifice and trades provide plentiful targets.
review_reason: Three-mana body with recurring artifact creatures; benefit needs a graveyard but the WB pool supplies many natural targets.

name: Pattern Buffer Preservation
rationale: Selection and graveyard setup with cheap beam-up; reuses ETBs and triggers grave-leave rewards at a modest tempo cost.

name: Relentless Drednok
rationale: Cheap artifact lifelinker supports lords, sacrifice and counters; graveyard cantrip prevents total irrelevance late.

name: Resistance Is Futile
rationale: Efficient nonartifact removal with a recursion alternative; numerous opposing Borg and ships constrain the kill mode.

name: Rogue Artificial Intelligence
rationale: Landcycling and modal ETB make six-mana body flexible; lacks evasion and has less value than the best expensive threats.

name: Salt Vampire
rationale: Lifelink two-drop supports racing and counters; hand disruption replaces the opponent's card rather than generating advantage.

name: Sela, Tal Shiar Paradox
rationale: Attacking self-enables tapped Romulan production from your graveyard; beam-up and exile effects add extra bodies.

name: Storied Veteran
rationale: Recurring two-power creature supports sacrifice and station; inability to block and finality reduce defensive value.

name: Stray from History
rationale: Two-card recursion has high late value; hand-exile mode and dilemma trigger improve usability before graveyard setup.

name: Tal Shiar Operative
rationale: Two-mana repeatable dilemma source; deathtouch makes attacks viable and surveil supports graveyard engines.

name: Tell Me What You See
rationale: Opponent controls the payoff; repeated bouncing spends mana for little board effect despite modal synergy.
review_reason: Opponent chooses the payoff; replay requires repeated two-mana investment and does not improve board position.

name: Tenacious Drone
rationale: Two useful artifact bodies across a trade; supports sacrifice, Borg lords and station efficiently.

name: Test of Loyalty
rationale: One-mana modal cantrip or Raise Dead; activates dilemma and grave-leave rewards but needs an existing graveyard card.

name: U.S.S. Reliant, From Hell's Heart
rationale: Immediate four-mana reanimation with eventual flying recursion; station ten is high, but the returned creature helps pay it.

name: Vengeance Mission
rationale: Global death drain gives reach to token sacrifice decks; three-mana noncreature setup is weak without substantial trading.

name: Academy Instructor
rationale: Noncreature casts produce Officers and grow the body; ships and beam-up recasts provide plentiful triggers.

name: Beckett Mariner, Impetuous Ensign
rationale: First strike makes a useful early attacker; station enables safe promotion triggers but three taps for two damage is slow.

name: Boarding Action
rationale: Hasty Klingon token supports sacrifice and eight power; beam-up repeats the body while consuming another creature's tempo.

name: Brazen Bluff
rationale: Opponent chooses the worse outcome for you; needs a noncreature spell on their stack and a worthwhile spell in hand.
review_reason: Punisher spell needs both an opposing noncreature spell and an advantageous free-cast option in hand; it cannot be valued as a reliable counterspell.

name: Cantankerous Captain
rationale: Self-pump gives a reasonable three-power attack; large board unlocks menace and improves token attacks or station power.

name: Captain James T. Kirk
rationale: Immediate token or filtering and repeatable modal attacks; grows a wide board and enables dilemma payoffs without other spells.

name: Captain Michael Burnham
rationale: Efficient trampler adds consistent landfall damage; fetchlands, New Planet creation and extra land plays enable counters.

name: Captain's Tutelage
rationale: Flash first strike can win combat and leave power; common instant removal makes the two-for-one risk substantial.

name: D-7 Battle Cruiser
rationale: Only three station counters unlock recurring hasty Klingons; token sacrifices feed black while further stationing unlocks flying.
review_reason: Station three unlocks repeated Klingon tokens before the final ship level; historical Synthesizer Labship and Lumen-Class Frigate validate early-level engines.

name: Dahar Master
rationale: Four-power creature converts spare artifact or token into two damage; often removes an opposing utility body.

name: Dominion Infiltration
rationale: Triple-red cost and temporary copies make it a poor recovery spell; strongest only with ETB targets or a finishing attack.

name: Encounter the Unknown
rationale: Instant sweep of small creatures is relevant against tokens; card-advantage mode prevents dead hands against larger threats.

name: Erica Ortegas, Plucky Pilot
rationale: Haste and temporary extra land accelerate landfall; bounced land helps future triggers but does not permanently ramp.

name: Exploratory Mission
rationale: Four-mana enchantment needs more land drops and spare casting mana; repeated resources are powerful only after setup.

name: Genesis Effect
rationale: Six damage kills most large creatures; costly but its Planet conversion adds fixing, graveyard fuel and landfall.

name: Horta
rationale: Landcycling preserves early usability; seven-power trampler is a reasonable finisher but six mana remains expensive.

name: Infinite Diversity
rationale: Nine mana plus a graveyard spell and a varied creature board is too much setup for most draft games.
review_reason: Nine mana plus graveyard spell plus federation board; the model sees copied spell upside but poorly captures three simultaneous setup requirements.

name: Khaaaaaaaaaaaannn!
rationale: Efficient scalable instant removal with exile; handles large creatures and prevents death recursion without extra setup.

name: Khan, Despot by Design
rationale: Large trampler plus asymmetric one-damage sweep punishes Borg and Officer tokens and small utility creatures.

name: La'An Noonien-Singh, Security
rationale: Four-power body helps meet eight power, then clears a blocker; double red and three toughness limit flexibility.

name: Lwaxana Troi, Charming Guest
rationale: Two-drop floor is acceptable; spending mana and tapping to double later triggers is slow and does not replay ETBs.

name: Munitions Enthusiast
rationale: Efficient three-power trampler with a death ping; trades up, stations well and punishes small blockers.

name: The Naked Time
rationale: Temporary ramp and a brief counter/haste window; compulsory land sacrifice can disrupt curve despite landfall synergy.

name: Pah-Wraith
rationale: Seven-mana haste finisher dramatically pumps a wide board; expensive and weak when drawn without creatures.

name: Perils of the Past
rationale: Instant combat pump or artifact destruction has unusually broad utility in a ship-and-Borg environment; modal trigger is a bonus.

name: Planetary Bombardment
rationale: One-mana removal hits many early engines; postcombat four-damage mode extends relevance against bigger bodies.

name: Planetary Patrol
rationale: Ordinary two-drop that attacks above rate on landfall turns; defensive size remains 2/2 without instant land entries.

name: Plasma Cascade
rationale: Three-damage instant with optional filtering; removes utility engines, supports graveyards and can finish opponents.

name: Q, Stacking the Deck
rationale: On-rate 4/4 turns later spare cards into repeated copies of one spell; impact depends on the randomly exiled card.

name: Quark, Humble Proprietor
rationale: Free artifacts feed sacrifice and artifact-count synergies, but prohibited Treasure sacrifice prevents ordinary ramp or fixing.
review_reason: Rules correction: cannot sacrifice Treasure tokens forbids every sacrifice use, not just their mana ability. Treasures mainly help Grand Nagus Zek, Worf, or Holo-Engineer.

name: Ravenous Cosmozoan
rationale: Discounted flying haste threat rewards spells and sacrificed artifacts; expensive when the graveyard is sparse.

name: Reckless Impulse
rationale: Efficient two-card access in a low curve; timing makes it worse when expensive cards or excess lands are revealed.

name: Red Alert!
rationale: Team power boost is narrow and often trades down; defensive discount does not add toughness or lasting value.

name: Sarcophagus, Ship of the Dead
rationale: Immediate anthem supports wide attacks and token trading charges the ship; ten counters still delay the flying body.

name: Savvy Profiteer
rationale: Two-mana ramp creature with two power; delayed Treasure activation fixes colors but competes with casting spells.

name: Silicate Surveyor
rationale: Solid reach body plus next-turn impulse card; useful ETB reuse and anti-air support, though five mana is crowded.

name: Starfleet Security
rationale: Cheap Officer and sacrifice fodder; death must occur on your turn and the Clue costs mana to realize.

name: Tal Shiar Analyst
rationale: Three-power station body with spell-based reach; lacks board control and noncreature chains rarely deal huge damage.

name: Targ Wrangler
rationale: Large menace attacker at three mana; recurring sacrifice requirement depletes resources unless supported by expendable tokens.

name: Tasha Yar, Out of Time
rationale: Hasty body trades into a card and a later replay; card access has timing limits but gives sacrifice decks resilience.

name: Test of Identity
rationale: Klingon double strike can finish or win combat; rummage mode avoids dead tribal cards and triggers dilemmas.

name: Transporter Malfunction
rationale: Two-mana three-damage spell to any target; expensive beam-up offers late reach and ETB reuse.

name: Will Riker, First in the Field
rationale: Four-power body plus temporary lands supports landfall and postcombat plays; no permanent ramp and limited immediate defense.

name: Worf, Intelligence Contractor
rationale: Temporary theft plus a solid body enables attack swings; sacrifice outlets turn the stolen small creature into permanent removal.

name: The Wrath of Khan
rationale: Three-mana four damage followed by filtering and an edict; usually produces immediate removal plus later resources.

name: Adversary by Algorithm
rationale: Three-mana artifact body from a spell supports both noncreature and Borg synergies; beam-up adds delayed reuse.

name: Amok Time
rationale: Fight plus later creature recursion offers value; needs a friendly creature initially and takes turns to recover the card.

name: Astute Terraformer
rationale: Reliable two-drop with a mana sink; distinct lands improve pump efficiency but it remains a ground creature.

name: Branching Timeline
rationale: Eight-mana payoff can produce many permanents; requires diverse lands and risks hitting lands when immediate stabilization is needed.
review_reason: Eight-mana spell often reveals only three to five cards including lands, with no guarantee of useful defensive bodies.

name: Captain Jonathan Archer
rationale: Efficient two-body play plus federation pump; his Human, Officer and Dog types alone provide a useful activation.

name: Captain Kathryn Janeway
rationale: Explores itself immediately and every later creature; counters, selection, lands and extra land drops support nearly every green plan.
review_reason: Immediate explore on a four-mana body and on every later creature supplies counters, selection and lands without another activation cost.

name: Captain Pike, Fullness of Time
rationale: Land access provides steady advantage and increasing body size; early stats and double-green cost depend on the mana base.

name: Cold-Blooded Crew
rationale: Flexible landcycler with counters to distribute; six-mana body bypasses small artifact blockers and supports Doctor payoffs.

name: Common Goal
rationale: Two-mana removal can combine two creatures' power; still requires a board and is vulnerable to instant removal.

name: Culber and Stamets, Star-Crossed
rationale: Four-mana 4/5 floor or useful mana rebate; modal ETB works well with beam-up and dilemma splashes.

name: Dathon and Picard at El-Adrel
rationale: Combat trick or nontoken artifact/enchantment edict; opponents choose the sacrifice and three mana is expensive.

name: David and Carol Marcus, Creators
rationale: Permanent fixing and ramp attached to a body; New Planet advances distinct-land count and is valuable to replay.

name: Dominion Assault Force
rationale: Efficient vigilant body with modal graveyard interaction or selection; strong station contribution after attacking.

name: Dominion Supervisor
rationale: Three-mana 4/2 floor with flexible counter placement; trample gives grown counter creatures a way through tokens.

name: Dr. Joseph M'Benga
rationale: Counter doubling and hexproof can dominate with support; four-mana 3/3 has no immediate bonus without another counter effect.

name: Dr. Leonard "Bones" McCoy
rationale: Flash creature plus broad non-Doctor recursion; protection mode and repeated beam-up provide useful flexibility.

name: Final Frontier
rationale: Finds dual Planets for ramp, fixing and diversity; beam-up repeats ramp and creature ETBs at a tempo cost.

name: First Contact
rationale: Instant selection finds most deck cards and fuels graveyards; no board development and occasional misses remain costs.

name: Genesis Device
rationale: Immediate ramp is reliable; late activation trades lands for better diversity and bursts of landfall, but costs five more mana.

name: Holo-Engineer
rationale: Six power across two bodies immediately; upgrades Officer/Borg output but converts Treasure, Food and Clue tokens into creatures too.

name: Hologram Stalker
rationale: ETB recursion immediately creates a 3/3 alongside the 2/2; continued grave-leave triggers generate more bodies, though six mana is slow.

name: I'm a Doctor, Not a . . .
rationale: One-mana untap trick leaves a counter; improves station and counter synergies while still risking removal in response.

name: Jadzia Dax, Living Legacy
rationale: Cheap scaling mana engine grows every first main phase; discard mode supplies counters when the body would be too slow.

name: Jake Sisko, War Correspondent
rationale: Ordinary early creature with incidental life; double-landfall turns add Clues but require fetchlands, ramp or extra land drops.

name: MACO Strike Team
rationale: Efficient early pressure and removal insurance for the team; tokens enter tapped, delaying station and defense.

name: Moopsy
rationale: Cheap deathtouch trades with grown threats and can cover fliers; one power offers little station or offensive pressure.

name: Mugato
rationale: Excellent five-mana size with vigilance and reach; difficult to attack through and provides six station power after attacking.

name: Neelix, Moral Support
rationale: Food and Planet lifegain can grow it; initially a weak 1/1 and realizing the first counter often costs extra mana.

name: Photosynthetic Physician
rationale: Solid reach finisher with graveyard token value; exile activation also triggers Vash or Hologram Stalker.

name: Rok-Tahk, Budding Scientist
rationale: Six-mana body and indestructible blocker are useful; abundant creature mana is less valuable once six mana has already been reached.
review_reason: Indestructible Murf is a real defensive benefit, but six-mana creature ramp arrives late and does not itself end the game.

name: Saru, Unthreatened
rationale: Flash body protects another creature from removal; useful reactive value and a respectable three-power station contribution.

name: Saurian Explorer
rationale: Landfall creates a substantial attacker; expensive repeatable Planet production helps long games but leaves defense unimproved.

name: Species 8472
rationale: Large stabilizer with lifegain and anti-artifact evasion; costs six and remains vulnerable to ordinary creature removal.

name: Stable Wormhole
rationale: Recurring land ramp feeds landfall but needs attacks and continued mana sinks; three-mana enchantment does not protect its caster.

name: Support Mission
rationale: Permanent counter engine has a strong long-game ceiling; spending three mana before deploying creatures loses substantial tempo.

name: Sylvia Tilly, Joy of Discovery
rationale: Surveil fuels immediate and repeated counter production; graveyard exile connects the counter and grave-leave strategies.

name: Syndicate Liquidators
rationale: Repeated permanent landfall counters make a large threat quickly; can give first counters to another creature for immediate combat impact.

name: Temporal Conqueror
rationale: Land recovery or Treasure plus a body supports fixing and graveyard play; beam-up can repeat both milling and advantage.

name: Test of Courage
rationale: Cheap artifact/enchantment removal has plentiful targets, but misses expensive ships and the graveyard mode is low impact.

name: U.S.S. Discovery, at Black Alert
rationale: Discover five gives immediate material and potentially a station creature; subsequent attacks repeat the effect for overwhelming advantage.
review_reason: Immediate discover five can supply the creature needed to station; repeated attack discovers are materially stronger than ordinary mana-ramp ship text.

name: U.S.S. Voyager, Lone Wanderer
rationale: Two lands immediately ramp and trigger landfall twice; station eight is steep for a 3/3 but secondary to the ETB.

name: Warp Speed
rationale: Searches to hand rather than ramping; untapped dual lands and late draw can help but initial board impact is minimal.
review_reason: Initial land goes to hand, not battlefield; later draw requires substantial mana and blue, so generic ramp/text features overstate its efficiency.

name: Xenobotanist
rationale: Two-mana fixing and ramp with three toughness; supports expensive bombs and splashes while surviving small damage.

name: Xindi Surveyors
rationale: Three-power creature grows permanently with land drops; common ramp and fetchlands can put it beyond damage removal.

name: All Good Things...
rationale: Three turns of cards and filtering, with possible ten life; five-mana setup is vulnerable before later chapters resolve.

name: Borg Cube
rationale: Affinity can make exile-plus-ship inexpensive; twelve station counters delay the stolen creature and flying anthem but removal is immediate.
review_reason: WB artifact creatures reduce cost and immediate exile matters even if station twelve is delayed; assimilation is not immediate on first entry.

name: The City on the Edge of Forever
rationale: Temporary reset plus cards and life; timing can let the opponent's army return first and token survival controls the lock.
review_reason: Opponent redeploys first after phasing; destroying the token and the timing of chapter-three sacrifice can return the opposing army before yours.

name: Cleveland Booker, Empath
rationale: Hybrid casting broadens playability; landfall produces attackers but the 2/2 body and nonblocking tokens are weak when behind.

name: Constable Odo
rationale: Hybrid five-drop offers either prolonged tempo or two Clues; modal ETB works with dilemma and beam-up engines.

name: Dal R'El, Augment Orphan
rationale: Efficient body turns land drops into extra mana and excess lands into cards; land sacrifice can undermine expensive finishers.

name: Daniels, Temporal Agent
rationale: Hybrid Gravedigger reuses premium creatures; putting itself under library triggers grave-leave synergies and gains life.

name: Dathon, His Heart Open
rationale: Three colors and enchantment density are demanding; saga acceleration is situational and a 3/3 alone does not justify the mana.

name: The Doctor, EMH
rationale: At worst a 5/5, with a potentially large team-counter burst; artifact typing and hybrid cost broaden synergy.

name: The Duras Sisters
rationale: Efficient hybrid three-power creature leaves a hasty Klingon after death; excellent for sacrifice and repeated trades.

name: D'Vana Tendi, Optimistic Ensign
rationale: Defensive body untaps lands, station creatures or utility abilities; optional surveil supports slower graveyard and ramp plans.

name: Gowron, Eager for Battle
rationale: Grows from either side's deaths; free Klingon sacrifice draws cards and trample lets growth translate into damage.

name: Gray and Adira, Forever Joined
rationale: Copying ETB creatures can generate significant value; four-mana 2/3 needs a precombat noncreature spell and a worthwhile creature.

name: Hemmer, Fixing What Is Broken
rationale: Efficient defensive body loots when stationing; ship hexproof only on your turn leaves opposing-turn removal live.

name: Hit It!
rationale: Team haste plus likely ramp supports landfall; spends a card without a creature and the five-card search can miss lands.

name: The Inner Light
rationale: Reanimation creates immediate value if the graveyard is stocked; later combat draw requires a successful connection.

name: Kira Nerys, Firebrand
rationale: Efficient trampler and token-attack interactions; limited ability to generate combat-speed creatures constrains its ceiling.

name: Kirk, Commanding Officer
rationale: Eight-power attacks generate impulse cards; solid body and sacrifice removal provide useful fallback roles.

name: Live Long and Prosper
rationale: Seven-mana life and hand doubling is poor with few cards left; no board impact and two-color cost limit recovery value.
review_reason: Seven-mana spell draws only current hand size and does not affect the board; usual late-game hand sizes undermine its ceiling.

name: Locutus, the One Who Speaks
rationale: Two-mana Borg lord scales every artifact creature; discard removal gives a strong fallback when the board is empty.

name: Lore, Positronic Provocateur
rationale: Hybrid artifact body with modal selection or evasion; reliable enabler for dilemmas and artifact synergies without huge raw impact.

name: L'Rell, Fierce Visionary
rationale: Produces a hasty Klingon every combat and can sacrifice it for surveil; recurring attacks and death synergies support the weak power.

name: Mirror Universe Intrusion
rationale: Three-mana clone with menace scales to the best enemy creature; kicked mode is powerful but costs nine total mana.

name: Nog, Ambitious Cadet
rationale: Cheap upgrade into a 3/4 menace body; tapping surveils and later graveyard land access supports sustained advantage.

name: Phlox, Unorthodox Doctor
rationale: Counter creatures become card-draw threats and trample improves connections; lacks an immediate counter on itself.

name: Sarek, Federation Ambassador
rationale: Usually draws zero or one card per combat after setup; three-color defensive body and five-type increments are demanding.
review_reason: Three-color 0/5 needs five non-Borg types per card; neither five creatures nor five lands substitutes for that requirement.

name: Seven of Nine
rationale: Dilemmas become cards, including repeatable Tal Shiar attacks; four-mana defensive body needs support but can generate immediate value.

name: Spock, Always Your Friend
rationale: Cheap body replaces itself in spell/ship-rich decks; chance of missing rises when creature count is too high.

name: The Traveler
rationale: Early reach/vigilance body scales with land diversity; three toughness limits durability and basic-heavy decks cap its power.

name: Vash, Freelance Archaeologist
rationale: Free upkeep surveil plus grave-leave card draw; inexpensive exile abilities and beam-up effects supply recurring triggers.

name: Worf, Honor-Bound Warrior
rationale: Hybrid creature can grow by tapping expendable artifacts and creatures; large attacks require both counters and total-power support.

name: Year of Hell
rationale: Symmetrical cards and damage are poor when behind; three-mana enchantment adds little unless racing or exploiting draw triggers.
review_reason: Three-mana symmetrical cards and damage give the opponent resources immediately; draw-trigger synergies do not usually justify the cost.

name: Zero, Incorporeal Sensate
rationale: Hybrid artifact lifelinker delays an opposing card with a two-mana tax; ETB reuse and counter placement improve its modest body.

name: Class-F Shuttlecraft
rationale: Three-mana fixing with a later vigilant flier; six station counters for two power is primarily a secondary benefit.

name: Combadge
rationale: Two equipment tokens support artifact count, but seven total mana to equip both makes unblockable setup slow and fragile.

name: Crystalline Entity
rationale: Eight-mana flier and nonartifact sweeper can turn a game around; opposing Borg and ships reduce the sweep's coverage.

name: Cybernetic Specialist
rationale: Colorless two-drop with selection and artifact typing; repeatable graveyard recycling triggers grave-leave payoffs without extra cards.

name: Deep Space 9
rationale: Nine-mana payoff has an enormous ceiling and immediate permanents, but is uncastable in many games and can hit mostly lands.
review_reason: Nine-mana card is uncastable in many GiH games, even though actual cast games can be spectacular.

name: Engineered Explosives
rationale: Flexible low-cost sweeper for tokens or selected mana values; constrained by colors and can destroy your own board.

name: The Holodeck
rationale: Seven-mana artifact requires further mana to gain value; sideboard access is legal in limited but too slow in typical games.
review_reason: Seven mana to deploy plus full costs for subsequent permanents; no immediate defensive or card return despite outside-game access.

name: Isolinear Processor
rationale: Restricted artifact ramp and looting support ships; cannot accelerate most creatures and has no defensive body.

name: Replicator
rationale: Copies useful creature tokens or Food for repeated resources; requires a suitable token and continuing mana investment.

name: Sickbay
rationale: Starts adding counters immediately in combat and scales with lifegain; five-mana artifact without its own body is a major liability.

name: Tea, Earl Grey, Hot
rationale: Cantripping artifact supports sacrifice, life and modal triggers; spends mana for no initial creature but is broadly playable glue.

name: Tricorder
rationale: Cheap reusable power and surveil; helps small evasive creatures and graveyards but loses tempo when the carrier is removed.

name: Type-2 Phaser
rationale: Immediate stun supplies tempo and later large power for evasion or station; three-mana equip is expensive.

name: U.S.S. Cerritos, Following Up
rationale: Two immediate Officers can help charge the ship; five mana for the initial board is weak without other station bodies.

name: U.S.S. Enterprise-D, Galaxy-Class
rationale: Low-cost ship gives impulse access on the first station each turn; eventually an efficient vigilant flier, with ongoing station activations still legal.
review_reason: Station remains usable after the ship is a creature, enabling repeated impulse cards; first-turn exiled card may still be uncastable.

name: Warp Core
rationale: Fixes a basic land to hand and accelerates ship counters; low initial board impact and narrow activated ability outside ship decks.

name: Andoria
rationale: Tapped blue-red fixing, lifegain and unique Planet name; useful for spell decks and green-based splashes.

name: Artificial Anomaly
rationale: Colorless land adds a distinct name and later drain plus New Planet; activation is modest and hurts early colored mana.

name: Bajor
rationale: Tapped red-white fixing and lifegain; useful but aggressive eight-power decks pay a real tempo cost.

name: Blood Crypt
rationale: Untapped fixing when needed supports early Klingons and removal; distinct name helps splashed land-diversity effects.

name: Breeding Pool
rationale: Flexible fixing and unique name strengthen the land-diversity archetype; life payment matters mainly against fast decks.

name: Cardassia Prime
rationale: Fixes the artifact deck and gains life; Planet typing permits green searches and supports counter/lifegain splashes.

name: Earth, Sector 001
rationale: Searchable dual Planet directly supports distinct lands; tapped entry is more acceptable in the slower blue-green plan.

name: Federation Outpost
rationale: Late untapped modal land adds dilemma triggers and selection or life; early tapped entry is its main cost.

name: Ferenginar
rationale: Tapped fixing and lifegain support a slower graveyard plan; searchability and unique name help multicolor green decks.

name: Gaseous Anomaly
rationale: Colorless early mana is costly; late two-card draw and Planet conversion provide a meaningful flood outlet.

name: Godless Shrine
rationale: Reliable early fixing for artifact lords and removal; life-payment flexibility is useful across aggressive and controlling builds.

name: Hallowed Fountain
rationale: Flexible fixing for early crews and removal; distinct name adds incidental land-diversity value.

name: Ni'Var Science Academy
rationale: Late untapped entry gives free selection or evasion and a dilemma trigger; early tapped land remains a tempo liability.

name: Orion
rationale: Searchable dual Planet supports landfall and splashes; tapped entry can delay pressure but life partially offsets the cost.

name: Overgrown Tomb
rationale: Flexible green-black fixing with a unique name; useful in multicolor graveyard/ramp decks without forcing a tapland.

name: Q Continuum
rationale: Modal land gives a free late counter-sized combat boost or selection; adds a distinct land name without losing colored mana.

name: Qo'noS
rationale: Tapped fixing and life; less attractive in the fastest Klingon starts but useful for consistent two-color mana.

name: Quark's Bar
rationale: Late selection or damage with a dilemma trigger; early tapped entry is a cost for pressure decks.

name: Risa
rationale: Fixing plus lifegain supports counter creatures and Doctors; searchable Planet name also contributes land diversity.

name: Romulus
rationale: Tapped fixing for dilemma creatures and interaction; stable mana supports the archetype's multicolor engines.

name: Sacred Foundry
rationale: Untapped fixing preserves aggressive curves at a life cost; less land-diversity synergy than green combinations.

name: Spatial Anomaly
rationale: Colorless land can become a removal spell and fixing later; high activation cost restricts timely use against engines.

name: Starfleet Academy
rationale: Colorless land with a costly federation mana ability; needs more than five creature types before producing a useful mana advantage.
review_reason: Five mana plus tapping the land requires more than six creature types for net mana growth; colored-mana opportunity cost remains.

name: Steam Vents
rationale: Flexible fixing for early spells and creatures; untapped option helps double-spell turns.

name: Stomping Ground
rationale: Flexible green-red fixing supports landfall curves and ramp; distinct name improves strange-new-worlds splashes.

name: Subspace Anomaly
rationale: Colorless land turns into two Officers plus a fixing Planet; useful late for station and counters but costly to activate.

name: Temple Garden
rationale: Flexible fixing preserves green-white curves and supports premium gold payoffs; incidental unique land name is valuable.

name: Temporal Anomaly
rationale: Late permanent selection and graveyard fuel replace the land with a fixing Planet; early colorless mana is the tradeoff.

name: Unexplored Territory
rationale: Fetchland adds diversity and a later landfall trigger, but activation costs one mana in addition to tapping itself.

name: The Unicomplex
rationale: Late modal land can recover a premium creature or surveil; supports dilemmas and grave-leave triggers without a spell slot.

name: Vulcan
rationale: Tapped dual Planet fixes the ship deck and gains life; searchable fixing also supports slower green splashes.

name: Watery Grave
rationale: Flexible untapped fixing for the modal deck's early curve; reliable casting outweighs modest life costs.

name: Plains
rationale: Basic-land estimate reflects the white deck population and cards seen, not a standalone spell-strength rating.

name: Island
rationale: Basic-land estimate reflects the blue deck population and cards seen, not a standalone spell-strength rating.

name: Swamp
rationale: Basic-land estimate reflects the black deck population and cards seen, not a standalone spell-strength rating.

name: Mountain
rationale: Basic-land estimate reflects the red deck population and cards seen, not a standalone spell-strength rating.

name: Forest
rationale: Basic-land estimate reflects the green deck population and cards seen, not a standalone spell-strength rating.
